To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have created a validation dataset of 64 cases with pathologist annotations of ROIs that are appropriate for estimating sTIL density and the sTIL values for those ROIs.
we have developed a method for creating a dataset that can be used to validate AI algorithms that process digital pathology images and that we have tested this method in a pilot study.

we have built workflows for collecting data for validating algorithms that process WSIs, we have demonstrated the feasibility of the workflows in a pilot study, and we will be refining the workflows and statistical methods in preparation for pivotal studies and sharing the dataset and methods with the digital pathology community.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a dataset for validating AI in digital pathology.
the creation and validation of a dataset for use by the AI community in developing algorithms that estimate the density of sTIls.
developing and validating algorithms that process WSIs and provide information that is useful for patient care and clinical research.

the project is a success in that we have created a validation dataset of 64 WSIs with annotations of the ROI type, sTIL density, and pathologist identity.
this work is an important step toward creating a dataset that is fit for regulatory purposes.
the dataset is a work in progress and that we are committed to making it as useful as possible.

it is a pathologist-annotated validation dataset that can be used to validate algorithms that process WSIs.
we are building a dataset that can be used to train and validate algorithms for the estimation of sTIL densities.
we are building a dataset to help accelerate the validation of algorithms for processing WSIs.

the creation of such a dataset is not trivial.
